title: Unsupervised Representation Learning - an Invariant Risk Minimization Perspective
claim: Supervised invariance models rely on labels in their causal graphs; ours drops labels and keeps only invariant and environment-dependent latents generating data.
layout: 4 panels in a row, left-to-right, labeled causal graphs, last one highlighted by removal of Y
description: Four small directed graphs are arranged in a row. Each has circular nodes with math labels and a bold caption below. The first three, Anti-Causal FIIF SCM, Causal FIIF SCM and Causal PIIF SCM, are the supervised cases. They contain a label node Y, an invariant latent Z_inv, an environment-dependent latent Z_e, an observed X, and a dashed environment node e. The arrows differ across the three graphs. In the anti-causal case Y points to both latents. In the causal FIIF case Z_inv points to Y, and Y points to Z_e. In the causal PIIF case Y has only an incoming arrow from Z_inv. The fourth panel, Unsupervised SCM, drops Y entirely. Only Z_inv and Z_e point to X, and e points to Z_e. Everything is black line art on white. The eye goes to the arrows and the four bold captions.
caption: IRM Generative Structural Causal Models for supervised (left $3$ figures) and unsupervised (right figure) cases
abstract: We propose a novel unsupervised framework for \emph{Invariant Risk Minimization} (IRM), extending the concept of invariance to settings where labels are unavailable. Traditional IRM methods rely on labeled data to learn representations that are robust to distributional shifts across environments. In contrast, our approach redefines invariance through feature distribution alignment, enabling robust representation learning from unlabeled data. We introduce two methods within this framework: Principal Invariant Component Analysis (PICA), a linear method that extracts invariant directions under Gaussian assumptions, and Variational Invariant Autoencoder (VIAE), a deep generative model that separates environment-invariant and environment-dependent latent factors. Our approach is based on a novel ``unsupervised'' structural causal model and supports environment-conditioned sample-generation and intervention. Empirical evaluations on synthetic dataset, modified versions of MNIST, and CelebA demonstrate the effectiveness of our methods in capturing invariant structure, preserving relevant information, and generalizing across environments without access to labels.
